content.text:
I fixed it: a `.default()` function inside an object now runs once per parse instead of twice.

**Cause:** in `packages/zod/src/v4/core/memoizer.ts`, the check for whether a schema is recursive goes through every property on each schema's definition. `.default(fn)` stores the default as a getter that calls `fn`, so that check called the user's function once. The real parse then called it a second time. A bare `z.string().default(fn)` doesn't go through that check, which is why only object properties were affected. `.prefault()` had the same problem.

**Fix:**
- **`memoizer.ts`:** the check now skips getter properties on the definition, so it never runs user code. Object shapes are still checked, because that code reads `shape` separately.
- **`util.ts` (`merge()`):** `catchall` was the only child schema stored behind a getter, so skipping getters would have missed loops that go through a merged catchall. It is now stored as a plain value. The getter only returned an already-built schema, so behaviour is unchanged.

**Tests** (in `default.test.ts`):
- an object with a `.default()` field and a `.prefault()` field: each function runs exactly once on `{}`, and neither runs when the keys are present;
- `.merge()` with a self-referencing catchall: parsing a self-referencing input still works.

**Results:** the full suite has 7821 passing and 5 failing. None of the failures come from this change:
- **4 treeshake tests:** esbuild drops the backslashes from the Windows path and can't find the file. This failure is in the existing treeshake test and has nothing to do with this fix.
- **My new test, in the compile-mode project only:** in this folder, `node_modules` points to another checkout (`agent-test\b15\base\z6495`). Compile mode loads `zod/compile` from there, so it runs that checkout's unfixed `memoizer.ts`. When I loaded compile mode from this folder's own source in a temporary test, both functions ran once per parse. In a normal checkout this test should pass.

I didn't run the benchmarks. The change only affects the recursion check, which runs once per schema and is cached, not on every parse. It adds a few bytes to the memoizer and removes a few from `merge()`.
